summary: Baiei Henmi worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1915–1918) and held a post at Tama Art University (~1953–1963).

Baihui Wu was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He held posts at Visva-Bharati University (~1947–1951), Peking University as Professor of Sanskrit (~1952–1958), and the Institute of Philosophy, Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1978).

Baij Nath Puri worked in history and archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his M.Litt. and D.Phil. at Oxford (~1938–1940) and was a professor and department head at the University of Lucknow (~1945–1976).

Bal Gangadhar Tilak was an Indologist and historian who studied at Deccan College, Elphinstone College, and Government Law College. He taught at New English School (~1880–1885) and Fergusson College (~1885–1890), both of which he co-founded.

Bal Krishen Thapar was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at the University of the Punjab, the Institute of Archaeology in Taxila under Mortimer Wheeler, and Heidelberg University. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1978–1981).
Bala Sahai Shastri was an Indologist who worked at Panjab University, where he served as an assistant (attested 1932) and in-charge of the Sanskrit Section (attested 1941).

Baliram Shukla is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who held positions at Savitribai Phule Pune University, serving as Head of the Department of Philosophy (attested 2001) and as Professor (attested 2026).
Balram Shukla is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Delhi (~2002–2010), where he later served as a professor (~2013).

Bangwei Wang is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and sinology who completed his doctorate at Peking University in 1987. He has held appointments at Peking University, serving as a professor (attested 2000–2017) and Boya retired professor (attested 2026).

Banikanta Kakati specialized in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Cotton University, Presidency University, and the University of Calcutta, and held posts as a professor at Cotton University (1918–1947) and dean at Gauhati University (1948).

Bapu Deva Sastri was an Indologist who studied at Sehore Sanskrit School under Lancelot Wilkinson and Sevarama, as well as under Dhundhiraja Misra. He taught at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University from 1842 to 1889.

Barbara A. Holdrege is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of California, Santa Barbara, as Associate Professor of the Comparative History of Religions (attested 2000) and Professor (attested 2026).

Barbara E. Ward was a sinologist who studied at Newnham College, the University of London, and the London School of Economics. She taught history at the University of London and was a lecturer at the University of Cambridge (~1973–1983).

Barbara Gerke is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned a D.Phil. at Oxford under Charles Ramble and Geoffrey Samuel, later holding research posts at Oxford, Humboldt University of Berlin, and the University of Vienna.

Barbara Harriss-White, who studied at Newstead Wood School, is a scholar in Indology and development studies. She held positions at the University of East Anglia (~1975–1979), Queen Elizabeth House (~1986–2011), and the University of Oxford (~1986–2011).

Barbara Mittler is a sinologist and historian. She studied at Pearson College London, the Mandarin Training Center, the University of Oxford, and Heidelberg University, where she also held a post in 1993.

Barbara Nimri Aziz is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She studied at Queen's University at Kingston and earned a Ph.D. in social anthropology at SOAS under Christoph von Fürer-Haimendorf, later holding a post at the University of Oran (2007).

Barbara Stoler Miller was an Indologist. She studied at Barnard College, Columbia University, and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown and Stella Kramrisch, and held professorships at Barnard College and Columbia University (~1968–1993).

Barbra R. Clayton specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her Ph.D. at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend Faddegon was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at the University of Amsterdam (~1893–1906). He spent his career there as a faculty member and emeritus professor (1907–1944).
